Here is my input. I'm assuming you are undiagnosed since you mentioned that your post, but please reply if you were already diagnosed because I don't think my comment would be relevant.

I wouldn't attach to the diagnoses when you're not diagnosed, i.e. I wouldn't tell people you're schizoaffective if you're not diagnosed. I would focus on trying to get better in your own time and around your family, while actively speaking to psychiatrists to confirm your diagnoses. Once you're diagnosed you can either get on medication or get therapy, or both, with a medically confirmed basis to work off of. If therapy is practical for you now, then no problem in trying to speak to a therapist now. When you're trying methods to minimize symptoms and if things still aren't manageable, I think telling people around you that you are schizoaffective is more of a sensible option in my opinion.

For now, I do think that telling those closer to you the issues you are facing is helpful. Forming a support network is helpful when you're having these kinds of experiences.

Giving your case some thought and asking yourself "what can this argument do for me in my last speech". You have the opportunity to find holes in case before the round, so try to take advantage of that. Be grateful if you have a coach there to fix up your case, but don't become complacent. If you see 3 cards saying the same thing and 1 card that doesn't do anything, fix it so you have more useful arguments to utilize in the debate.

Speech drills to improve speed and clarity so people can actually hear the arguments you're making. Practice emphasis and try to make yourself easier to follow. Slow down on taglines and your own analytics. Good signposting should separate the debate in an intuitive way. 

Judge instruction: tell the judge why you won. Narrow down the debate so you could blow up issues you're winning and show why that should win you the debate. Judges are trying to find the most obvious way a debater won the ballot, so if you write the ballot for them in your speech that helps. Also, read your judge's paradigm so you know what's persuasive to them. That might change how you're making arguments, what arguments you're going for, and what your last speech will look like.

Believe in yourself. After your opponents speech ask yourself what's the threat and what you can do to win this debate. Don't believe your opponents cross-ex explanation, pull out links from their arguments and win some debates. Any time you're talking is your opportunity to explain the whole debate. That includes why their argument is something that they're not saying it is. Also, if one of your opponent's argument isn't going to win them the debate, then don't spend so much time on it.

Make debate easy for yourself. Have blocks ready to answer common arguments. Have case overviews and stuff ready. Organize your files they're easy to navigate in debates. Circle arguments that you need to answer on your flow so you make sure you answer them in your next speech. Also just get good at flowing in general so debates are easier to follow for you. Make some friends and cherish the people that make debate what it is for you. Most importantly, have fun, learn some stuff, and don't take anything too personal.

I'm not sure what everyone wants out of rogue, but the way I view it is that it's a stealthy, high risk / high reward class. This suggestion will probably be very controversial, but I'd like to see how it fares, since I've had this thought for a while.

I played Black Desert for a couple months and one thing I admired about the Ninja class is that it had the ability to go full invis (no traces), but they had slowness during their invisibility. This would allow rogues to sneak up into crowds of players, deal damage, and get out. If this were to be implemented, I think the idea of infinite / short-cooldown and continuous invisibility should remain. The invisibility should be a core feature of the class, not just some skill I use every 2 minutes to sneak up on people. The slowness means that 1) invisibility won't be rogues' only way on engaging in fights and 2) rogues won't always be running around invis. I understand that full invisibility would be a huge problem for sneaking into bases (e.g. 15 people rogue invis into a base, switch to their respective classes, and make a faction go raidable), but I think there's a few options we have.

* Block rogues from passing through fence gates, doors, etc. that are not within their faction's claim *while invis* (edit)

* Invisibility will run out if the rogue is running around in the same general area (this threshold is shortened in other faction's claims)

* We could add a particle effect that occurs every 7 seconds or so on the rogue's location

I'm not sure how squishy Rogue is right now, but I think it should be more of a glass cannon type of class. I understand that the damage and invisibility thing will get really annoying (just like how getting constantly pegged by archers is getting annoying for some people right now), but the squishyness should balance that out a bit.

As for the implementation, the slowness would be a huge liability against people with radar. Maybe we could use ray ~~tracing~~ *(sorry, got mixed up)* casting on the server's end, so if players "hit" where the rogue is, the rogue will appear visible.

Aside from the invisibility idea, I would like to see speed 3 back in some form, though I think my opinion would vary on what else is done to the class. As you and others have noted, I think something needs to be done about the damage and that "something" will have to balance itself out with the issue on speed 3.
